claims.finding: On 2026-08-04 a federal jury in Boston (Judge Patti Saris) returned the first Covidien hernia-mesh bellwether verdict against Medtronic — $88m, $77m to Larry Patterson and $11m to his wife, on failure-to-warn over Symbotex mesh, with no punitives and no fraud finding — and that verdict sits on top of roughly 2,400 federal MDL cases, about 7,450 Massachusetts state cases and a coordinated Minnesota action with no global settlement in place.
claims.why_not_priced: Medtronic filed no 8-K on the verdict — the only filing between 2026-06-18 and the print is a DEFA14A on 2026-08-17 — and no captured earnings preview mentions litigation at all; the FY2026 10-K was filed 2026-06-18, seven weeks before the verdict, so the contingencies note the market last read predates it, and the FQ1 10-Q that follows this print is the first document that has to restate the exposure. If it were priced, the stock would not be sitting 4.6% higher over twenty days with a 21% realised vol and previews framing the quarter as 'confidently ready' for the US robotics push.
claims.independence: A second outlet carried the same verdict independently: https://www.startribune.com/jury-federal-bellwether-medtronic-covidien-mesh-hernia-88-million/601874963 — it appears in the skipped list of snapshots/20260830T152925Z.json with a fetch failure, so I have the URL slug and nothing more, but it is a different publisher naming the same federal bellwether and the same $88m.

claims.finding: FDA issued an Early Alert on Medtronic's and Given Imaging's Bravo esophageal pH monitoring capsule delivery device: Medtronic sent affected customers a quarantine letter on 2026-08-06 and, as of 2026-08-10, had reported 184 serious injuries and no deaths, and separately removed the Harmony pulmonary valve delivery catheter system after a 2026-05-28 customer letter over tip detachment.
claims.why_not_priced: This is a primary FDA page, published three and a half weeks before the print, that no captured preview or sell-side note references; Medtronic filed no 8-K about it. 184 serious injuries is a large enough count to seed follow-on product liability even though the Bravo line is immaterial to revenue, and a company that had seen the market price this would not have gone into the print with previews discussing only growth drivers.
claims.independence: Trade press covered the same recall separately: https://www.medtechdive.com/news/medtronic-recalls-ph-monitoring-capsule-linked-to-184-serious-injuries/829038/ (body stored, docs/2edb580f0dd2d292f6dec88e4ab4151efd4c407e.txt), and the Harmony catheter removal has its own FDA page at https://www.fda.gov/medical-devices/medical-device-recalls-and-early-alerts/pulmonary-valve-catheter-delivery-system-recall-medtronic-removes-harmony-delivery-catheter-system
